newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE MAS SAYS NO ORDER TO MERGE BANK TRANCHES.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE MAS SAYS NO ORDER TO MERGE BANK TRANCHES.

text.p: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on Friday it has no intention of asking banks to merge their local and foreign share tranches.

"MAS would like to clarify that it has no intention to require banks listed on the Stock Exchange of Singapore to merge their local and foreign tranches," a spokesman from the de facto central bank told Reuters.
The MAS spokesman was responding to queries by Reuters.
He said the need for dual listings depended on the company's limits on foregn shareholdings.
"Such limits are matters for companies themselves to decide," he said.
Dealers said there was a lot of confusion in the market after rife speculation that banks could make changes to the foreign shareholdings of their stock.
The daily Business Times said on Friday that a straw poll among companies with dual listing suggested that many would prefer any move to abolish the dual listing to come from the authorities.
Under current Singapore laws, foreigners can hold up to 40 percent of bank shares.
Shares of Singapore's big four banks, namely DBS Bank, OCBC Bank, United Overseas Bank and Overseas Union Bank have separate quotations for their local and foreign tranches.
